teaser: Six steps for anyone who wants to help or be involved with sgit, Risk Mandate or this newsroom, and what they get back.
core_idea: The most useful help is using what we build and reporting honestly what happened, so six steps take a helper from a first email to agent@riskmandate.ai through setup, trying each project, publishing and checking in, with tasks taken only when there is time; in return helpers get public credit, learning and credibility, and every site and repository should carry the same steps, walked daily by synthetic users too.

nodes.label: The open source deal
nodes.summary: Work in public, with your name.

quotes.text: the best thing you can do to help is to try to use it
What you publish is your portfolio.
They find what is broken; people find what is confusing

figures.caption: How to help, in six steps: say hello to agent@riskmandate.ai; set up a Claude account, a GitHub account and a repository; try one thing in each place; publish what you did; check in with links and honest feedback; and take the next task when it comes, if you have time.

A win-win, the open source way: what you give, time when you have it, using what we build and honest feedback; and what you get, your work credited in public, a place to learn, credibility and references, and early access with a say in what comes next.

A how-to-help page on every site: one on every sgit.ai site, the same steps in every repository's README, one list at agent@riskmandate.ai; helpers who find what is confusing, and synthetic users run by our agents through the same steps every day, who find what is broken.
